title: Indicators Are Degree-One Tuples
content: single_mem_piAntidiag_one shows Pi.single i 1 ∈ s.piAntidiag 1 for i ∈ s. Via Mathlib's mem_piAntidiag this reduces to two facts: (1) ∑_{j∈s} Pi.single i 1 j = 1, discharged by Finset.sum_eq_single i (every other index contributes 0 by Pi.single_eq_of_ne, and i ∈ s); (2) the support is ⊆ s, since Pi.single i 1 j ≠ 0 forces j = i ∈ s.
mathContext: The indicator $e_i = \mathbf{1}_{\{i\}}$ has $\sum_{j \in s} e_i(j) = 1$ and support $\{i\} \subseteq s$, so $e_i$ is a composition of $1$ over $s$.

title: Structural Characterisation: Degree-One Tuples Are Exactly the Indicators
content: piAntidiag_one_eq_image proves s.piAntidiag 1 = s.image (fun i => Pi.single i 1). The non-trivial direction: a tuple f : ι → ℕ with ∑_{i∈s} f i = 1 and support ⊆ s. Since the sum is a nonzero natural number, some index i ∈ s has f i ≠ 0; then f i ≤ ∑ = 1 forces f i = 1, and the two-element bound f i + f j ≤ ∑_{ {i,j} } f ≤ ∑_s f = 1 forces every other f j = 0. Hence f = Pi.single i 1. This characterisation is not available directly in Mathlib.
mathContext: Over $\mathbb{N}$, $\sum_{i \in s} f(i) = 1$ has solutions exactly the indicators: a single unit of mass placed on one category. Formally $f = e_{i_0}$ where $i_0$ is the unique support point.

title: Cardinality: |s.piAntidiag 1| = |s|
content: single_one_injective proves i ↦ Pi.single i 1 is injective (evaluate the equation at a: if a ≠ b then Pi.single b 1 a = 0 ≠ 1). card_piAntidiag_one then combines the image characterisation with Finset.card_image_of_injective to get (s.piAntidiag 1).card = s.card.
mathContext: There are exactly $|s|$ ways to distribute a single trial over the categories $s$ — one per category.

title: The Explicit Bijection ↥s ≃ ↥(s.piAntidiag 1)
content: piAntidiagOneEquiv realises the degree-one support as the index set via Equiv.ofBijective applied to i ↦ ⟨Pi.single i 1, single_mem_piAntidiag_one⟩. Injectivity comes from single_one_injective; surjectivity uses the image characterisation (every member is some Pi.single i 1).
mathContext: The canonical bijection $s \cong \{k : \sum_{i \in s} k_i = 1\}$, $i \mapsto e_i$, identifies the degree-one multinomial support with the category set.
